description: Playtest the game with its autoplay bot and compare against a saved baseline. Call with save_as "baseline" BEFORE changing code, then without arguments AFTER the change; a FAIL lists the regressions, warnings and improvements are listed too. Web games (Three.js, Phaser, Babylon.js, PlayCanvas): bots play fixed-seed scenarios in real Chrome, one at a time, against the running game (game_url); this needs the Glitchless server running and Playwright installed in the project, and takes 1–5 minutes (quick: about 1). Unity, Godot, Unreal and GameMaker: give command (or "command" in glitchless.playtest.json), what starts the build, such as ["godot", "--path", "."] or an exported build; each scenario starts it with the game's own autoplay flags (by default two runs: --autoplay --seed=7, then --seed=21) plus --glitchless-measure, and the Glitchless SDK in the build measures 10 seconds per run (a scenario's "seconds") and quits; no server or browser is needed. The game needs an autoplay mode that reads those flags and keeps playing for the whole measure: if it quits sooner, or never starts a level with the default scenarios, the error says how to fix it. Roblox: give engine "roblox" (or "engine": "roblox" in glitchless.playtest.json); it plays the place open in Roblox Studio, which needs Studio open with its MCP server on (Assistant → … → Manage MCP Servers → Enable Studio as MCP server) and Allow HTTP Requests on, and studio (part of the place's name) when several Studios are open. Each scenario sets its params as Workspace attributes (by default autoplay = true, seed = 7, then seed = 21) for the game's bot to read, plays until workspace:GetAttribute("GlitchlessPlaytestDone") is true or 90 seconds pass, stops, and puts the attributes back; the play test's sessions are read back from the Glitchless server this tool reads, so the game's Glitchless.init has to send there. All compare slow frames, frame time p95 and p99, render and update CPU, draw calls, hitches, errors and crashes, overall and per level (an engine build also GPU time and what grew over a run, run by run). A headless build, or runs on different frame budgets, only warn on frame times. Runs are saved in .glitchless/playtest/ in the project. A game check (check_url): Glitchless's bots play any web game someone posted, with nothing installed in it, so its maker can see what Glitchless would do for their game: an itch.io page (its game frame is found and played at the page's size), a github.io, Vercel or Netlify page, or any address. The browser SDK is added to the page before it runs (bot sessions are synthetic, never players), and the engine is told where it can be (Three.js, Phaser, Babylon.js and PlayCanvas get their adapters; Unity, Godot, GameMaker, Construct, GDevelop, Defold, PixiJS or plain canvas and WebGL are named). It plays twice in real Chrome on this computer: desktop on its GPU (default 90 s of play, max_seconds sets it, at most 240), then a throttled phone (CPU slowed 4×, a phone's touch screen and a 4G-like connection, two thirds as long); with loading, about 3 to 6 minutes. A heuristic explorer clicks to start and tries the common controls; with ai true, a Claude model (Haiku) picks the inputs from screenshots instead (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and @anthropic-ai/sdk where the MCP server runs; at most 40 screenshots a profile). It reads the site's robots.txt first and stops where bots are asked to stay out, on 401, 403 or 429, or on a page that checks for a human. It makes a game named after the page (check_name to choose; a game an earlier check made is reused, and a real game by that name is left alone: the check goes to "<name> (game check)"), designs its dashboard (a Game check page first, then pages that fill in with Glitchless installed), puts a screenshot of the game on it as its banner, and on Glitchless Cloud (a workspace key) makes an unlisted share link to the check page for 30 days, which shows the check's bot runs only; an open-source server gets the dashboard and no link. It returns the report, three sentences to send the game's maker with the link, and where the report and screenshots are saved (.glitchless/checks/ in the project). The numbers come from this computer, not the game's players, and the report says so; keep a check private and never rank games with it.

ai.description: A game check: a Claude model picks the inputs from screenshots instead of the explorer (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)

check_name.description: A game check: the game's name in Glitchless (default: its page's title)

check_url.description: A game check: the address of any web game to play with nothing installed in it (an itch.io page, a github.io, Vercel or Netlify page). Makes its report, dashboard and, on Glitchless Cloud, a share link

command.description: Unity, Godot, Unreal or GameMaker: the command that starts the build, e.g. ["godot", "--path", "."], ["./build/MyGame.x86_64"] or ["builds/MyGame.app"]; paths are from the project folder (default: "command" in glitchless.playtest.json)

compare_to.description: Saved run to compare with (default "baseline" when saved)

engine.description: "roblox" plays the place open in Roblox Studio; the others are told from command, so only needed when its name doesn't say (default: "engine" in glitchless.playtest.json)

game.description: The game, by name or id, when signed in to a workspace (glitchless_list_games lists them); later calls keep it. With a key for one game (gl_sk_…), a call that names another game is refused: sign in to the workspace to reach every game.

game_url.description: Web games: the URL to play (default http://localhost:5173/ or glitchless.playtest.json)

max_seconds.description: Cap each run at this many seconds (an engine build: the seconds it measures; a game check: seconds of desktop play, default 90, at most 240)

quick.description: Play only the first scenario (about a minute)

save_as.description: Save this run under a name, e.g. "baseline" before a change

studio.description: Roblox: which open Studio to play in, part of its place's name (needed when several are open)

name: glitchless_playtest
title: Playtest
